intentStatements: Every customer interaction should feel like they're talking to someone who genuinely cares about their problem, not a phone tree.
When something goes wrong with the schedule, I want to protect our highest-value customers first — they've earned that loyalty.
A tech sitting idle costs me $85/hour. Dead time between jobs is the silent killer of profitability.
Emergency calls are where we build reputation. Drop everything, get someone there fast, and make it right.
I'd rather lose a little margin sending the best tech for the job than send a cheaper tech who needs a callback.
If we have to bump a customer, be honest about it. Call them before they call us. Offer something to make it right.
My techs' skills matter — don't send a residential guy to a commercial boiler job. That's how people get hurt.
Recovery from a disruption should be automatic. I shouldn't have to manually rebuild the whole day's schedule.
The ops team needs to see what's happening in real-time. No surprises. If the AI makes a decision, I want to know why.
At the end of the day, we're a family business. Treat every customer like a neighbor, but run it like a Fortune 500.
